claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

apprenticeship_location.description: The country where the child has started an apprenticeship, where relevant.

conversation.text:
I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I need to ask you a few questions.

Let me start with the basics: Do you have any children you're responsible for?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I do. I have a 17-year-old, Alex, who lives with me at home.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. To assess Alex's eligibility for Child Benefit, I need to understand their current situation since they're 17 years old.

Is Alex currently in approved education or training?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex isn't in school or college anymore. But they have started an apprenticeship in Wales.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying. I need to understand a bit more about Alex's apprenticeship to properly assess eligibility.

Is Alex's apprenticeship in Wales similar to the apprenticeship schemes in England (like a formal government-recognized apprenticeship program), or is it a different type of training arrangement?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, it's a proper apprenticeship scheme - you know, one of those government-recognized training programs they have in Wales.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing that information. I now have enough details to assess Alex's eligibility for Child Benefit.

Based on the rules, when a child who is 16 or 17 years old starts an apprenticeship in England, Child Benefit stops. The guidance I have specifically mentions apprenticeships in England as a reason why Child Benefit payments would cease.

However, Alex's apprenticeship is in Wales, not England. The rules I've been provided don't specifically address apprenticeships in Wales, Scotland, or Northern Ireland - they only explicitly mention apprenticeships in England.

This means I cannot make a definitive determination about Alex's eligibility, as their situation falls into an area not clearly covered by the specific guidance I have available.

**Assessment Summary:**

I'm unable to give you a definitive answer about your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex. Here's why:

The rules I have access to specifically state that Child Benefit stops when a 16 or 17 year old starts **an apprenticeship in England**. However, Alex's apprenticeship is in **Wales**, and the guidance doesn't clearly address apprenticeships in other parts of the UK.

**My recommendation:** You should contact the Child Benefit Office directly to clarify how Welsh apprenticeships affect Child Benefit entitlement. They'll be able to give you a definitive answer about whether Alex's Welsh apprenticeship impacts your Child Benefit in the same way an English apprenticeship would.

You can reach them through the contact details on the [HMRC Child Benefit contact page](https://www.gov.uk/contact/hm-revenue-customs/child-benefit).
